hypothesis: The complete v25 live portfolio can produce mechanically valid protected lifecycles while causal eligible-signal, one-blocker, and aligned-orderbook telemetry identifies exact provider-symbol conditions that clear measured live friction.
decision: Keep the running v25 strategy and both protected open lifecycles unchanged. Do not loosen a blocker or add orderbook-pressure authority: none of the 50 one-blocker route-horizon comparisons with at least three non-overlapping resolved paths had positive mean return after the 13-bps friction estimate, and none of the 23 L2 aligned-versus-opposed comparisons with at least three paths per side had positive aligned mean return after friction. L2 alignment was relatively better in 19 comparisons, so retain it as descriptive research telemetry rather than discard it or promote it. Reconcile the actual SOL and GOLD exits before evaluating provider-specific exit or sizing changes.
falsifier: A larger profile-matched forward sample with independently resolved, repeated positive after-friction paths would overturn the current no-promotion decision. Any lifecycle, fill, fee, funding, event-identity, authority, or evidence-hash inconsistency would invalidate this prefix and lower confidence.
limitations: Only four eligible evaluations and one closed current-run trade exist, so current-profile edge, win rate, drawdown, and income remain unestimated.
SOL and GOLD remain open; their marked PnL, MFE, MAE, and profit-protection state are provisional and excluded from closed performance.
One-blocker and L2 paths assume no orders or fills and subtract an estimated 13-bps round trip; they are opportunity diagnostics rather than executable PnL.

The 50 one-blocker comparisons reuse route events across fixed horizons; comparison count is not trade count, and only each bucket's non-overlapping count is treated as independent within that horizon.
All-time HT-Breakout statistics combine compatible live history but include more than the current process run and do not establish current-profile expected return.
L2 alignment being relatively less negative does not establish a positive filter, gate, ranking, or sizing edge.
The v25 process predates staged v26 HIP-3 telemetry repairs, so missing HIP-3 HA and order-block values cannot be interpreted as v26 behavior.
